mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declined by at least 0.1 percentage points, the 20-day forward return is negative, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, triggering hawkish monetary policy that depresses equity valuations over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of months where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, the 5-day forward return is positive, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market tightening, which precedes monetary policy tightening and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of months where PAYEMS increased and UNRATE decreased, the 20-day forward return is positive, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a housing starts decline (HOUST < 500) signals housing sector weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as economic slowdown risks rise.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, when HOUST < 500, the 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the signal in that regime over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) signals manufacturing contraction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as economic growth risks increase.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of months where INDPRO < 95.0, the 20-day forward return is positive, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals consumption-driven growth, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of months where RSAFS increased and HOUST decreased, the 60-day forward return is negative, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past month predicts negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days, as higher unemployment signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings potential.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of months where UNRATE increased by at least 0.1 percentage points, the 5-day forward return is positive, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1 QoQ > 2.0%) signals strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 QoQ > 2.0%, the 20-day forward return is negative, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
